title: vendor provenance scorecard pilot and empirical fallback cost accelerator
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: procurement and platform teams repeatedly ask for a defensible, repeatable way to quantify vendor provenance and the operational cost of switching models. We lack a lightweight, empirical score that combines availability, latency stability, quantization compatibility, licensing friction, and historical failure modes. Objective: deliver a pilot-grade Vendor Provenance Scorecard plus an "Empirical Fallback Cost Accelerator" that can simulate switching cost under real traffic mixes and produce procurement trigger thresholds. Scope: 1) define a minimal, auditable rubric (signals, weights, sampling) that can be calculated from existing telemetry and public metadata; 2) implement a pilot scoring pipeline that ingests telemetry, model metadata, and license/terms-parsing outputs; 3) build a simulation harness to run fallback scenarios (percent traffic shifted, capacity limits, quantFallback) against historical traces; 4) expose results in a dashboard and an alerts feed with clear procurement thresholds and suggested mitigations. Success metrics: scorecard computed for top 12 vendors, simulation accuracy within +/-15% vs small-scale switching experiments, two procurement triggers defined and validated by sales/solutions. Deliverables: PRD, rubric spreadsheet, scoring pipeline (ETL + compute), simulation notebook, Looker dashboard, alerting rules, and a short internal playbook for Sales/Support on how to use outputs.
comments: 2026-03-11 - Ava Chen: Kickoff complete. Interviewed Procurement (Lina Morales) and Solutions (Kofi Mensah). Key ask: a single actionable number that non-technical stakeholders trust. Procurement emphasized license parsing and indemnity flags as high priority.

We discussed trade-offs: heavy instrumentation improves fidelity but delays pilot — leaning toward a hybrid approach using sampled telemetry plus model metadata enrichment.
